**Finding submitted: deviation (high severity, T4C).**

**What the document does:**
- **§ 4.1 (p0024)** — one-year term, auto-renewing annually, terminable by *either* Party on 90 days' written notice effective at an anniversary. On notice period and on HDI's end-of-term-only convenience right, this **sits at our fallback** and I did not redline it.
- **§ 4.2 (p0026, p0029)** — but if *the Company* terminates, it owes a "Termination Payment" of 50% of trailing twelve-month Net Sales above $800,000, payable in eight quarterly installments.

**Why it fails the fallback:** fees to HDI are only 30% of Net Sales above $11,000/month (§ 3.1), so the termination formula can readily exceed a full year of fees — well beyond the fallback ceiling of three months' fees. The result is that the Company's nominal convenience right is not penalty-free, which is the substance the rule protects.

**Redline (validated, ok:true):** a proviso capping the Termination Payment at three months' fees under § 3.1. I used the **fallback rather than preferred** (no penalty at all) because HDI carries the site build and programming costs and the deal is a revenue share — deleting the payment outright would be disproportionate to the existing bargain.
